text.title: Project-Spec Structure Core Rules
text.summary: 12 testable rules every project-spec/ MUST satisfy: directory shape, routing pairs, the rebuild test and when it runs, same-PR delta updates, and the canonical location. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: project-spec/ MUST be a directory containing both flat reference files and routing subdirectories — never a single .md file.
rule.rationale: One file collapses under its own weight past ~500 lines; agents load the whole thing per query. Subfolders let routing be selective.

rule.statement: Each subdirectory MUST contain its own AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md routing pair before any content file is added.
rule.rationale: Per-module coverage rule (workspace convention). Skipping the routing doc forces bulk-load and erases the selective-read benefit.

rule.statement: project-spec/ + ui-ux-design.md + constitution.md MUST contain enough information that a mid-level dev (unfamiliar with the codebase) can rebuild the project in two weeks.
rule.rationale: The two-week ceiling forces concrete contracts and removes "we just know how it works" tribal knowledge. Mid-level is the calibration target because senior devs paper over gaps with experience.

rule.statement: Run the rebuild test at end-of-feature, immediately before moving the feature folder to done/, AND before each deploy that follows a CR or BUG fix. Never on a calendar cadence.
rule.rationale: The feature is the unit that mutates project-spec. Catching gaps at the boundary is the cheapest fix point. CR/BUG changes often patch a missing business rule or undocumented edge — the spec must absorb the lesson before the deploy goes out, not after.

rule.statement: Failing the rebuild test BLOCKS feature promotion to done/ and BLOCKS post-CR/BUG deploy.
rule.rationale: Soft enforcement turns the test into a ritual; hard enforcement keeps the spec live.

rule.statement: Any project-spec/ change required by a feature MUST be committed in the same PR that ships the feature code.
rule.rationale: Follow-up PRs vanish under "I will do it later" and the spec drifts. Same-PR ties code and contract atomically.

rule.statement: If a feature genuinely has no spec impact (pure perf tweak, copy fix, internal refactor with unchanged contract), readiness.md MUST state "no spec impact" with a one-line reason.
rule.rationale: The escape hatch is intentional but loud. Forcing a reason flushes out features that the author thinks have no impact but actually do.

rule.statement: Reviewer MUST check the spec diff against the code diff; mismatches block merge.
rule.rationale: The author has a blind spot — they wrote the code and the spec from the same mental model. A second pair of eyes catches the gap.

rule.statement: project-spec/ MUST live at `.aidocs/project-spec/` in the project repository, committed to git.
rule.rationale: A fixed path makes the spec discoverable by convention — any agent or tool finds it without reading constitution.md first. Git provides versioning, backup, review and multi-machine sync for free; a spec outside the repository lives on one machine and silently diverges.

rule.statement: The working tree keeps ONLY the current revision of every spec file — no `old/` folders, no `*-v2.md` copies, no changelog inside project-spec/.
rule.rationale: project-spec/ is the snapshot from which an identical product can be rebuilt. History belongs to git and to the feature/CR deltas under features/done/ — duplicating it inside the tree buries the current truth.

rule.statement: For a product spanning several repositories, keep ONE project-spec/ in `.aidocs/project-spec/` at the umbrella or monorepo root; nested repos MUST NOT carry their own copy.
rule.rationale: The spec describes the whole product, not one repo. Two copies means two truths; the loser drifts within weeks.

rule.statement: A project that keeps the spec anywhere else MUST declare the path in constitution.md under a "Project-spec location" heading; absence of a declaration means the canonical path applies.
rule.rationale: Legacy layouts exist. An explicit declaration keeps them navigable while the default stays zero-configuration.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit a project-spec/ tree passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold.

rule.statement: Skip; the project is a one-off script, throwaway prototype, or pure plumbing with no durable domain model — overhead exceeds value.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
